title: Regional latency deep-dive (edge scrapbook) - Nov 06 2029
content:
Summary:
- This is a working log for the regional latency anomaly that started 2029-11-02 and flared up during peak hours on Nov 5. The symptom set: elevated 95th/99th token latency and occasional request timeouts in EU-West and APAC edge clusters while US regions remained nominal.

Observed signals (quick hit):
- 95th token latency rose from baseline 45ms -> 180-300ms for batched short requests (seq len <64) between 08:30-11:30 UTC on 2029-11-05.
- Tail timeouts (request level) correlated with higher queue depths on edge balancers (avg queue depth 7 -> 24).
- GPU utilization on affected nodes hovered ~60-70% (not saturated), but context-switch counter and kernel-reload events spiked.
- Autoscaler triggered additional pods but warmup latency for KV cache loading increased cold-start penalties.
- Regional egress quiesce observed in EU-West zone 2 around 09:12 UTC (short network flaps seen on NIC telemetry).

Attendees (ran syncs Nov 6):
- Priya (owner)
- Liam (scheduling/serving runtime)
- Zoe (observability/console)
- Daniel (infra networking)
- Aisha (SRE on-call)
- Ops pager rotation (notes pasted from #ops-incident-eu)

Timeline (condensed):
- 2029-11-02: Small latency jitter observed, first ticket INFRA-3245 opened.
- 2029-11-04: Spike recurrence, initial hypothesis: preemption/backfill causing pack/unpack thrash.
- 2029-11-05 08:30 UTC: Major spike across EU-W and APAC edges, increased timeouts.
- 2029-11-05 09:15 UTC: Short NIC-related link flaps in EU-West zone 2 (device counters).
- 2029-11-05 10:00-12:00 UTC: Autoscaler oscillation between scale+warmup and scale-down; cold cache penalty amplified latencies.
- 2029-11-06: Deep-dive sync, reproduced locally with a micro-benchmark.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Scheduling jitter + kernel reloads: when new pods are scheduled on nodes with mixed kernel binaries (after recent node image roll), serving runtime triggers per-pod kernel selection path that causes extra device warmup and KV cache rehydration. Explains kernel-reload spike.
2) Edge balancer queueing + rate bursts: bursty client patterns hit per-route concurrency defaults, queue depth grows -> longer batching windows and higher 95/99 latency.
3) Transient network flaps causing retries and duplicate inflight work (observed NIC counters in EU-West).
4) Subtle device-level firmware regression reducing DMA throughput under certain fragmentation patterns (lower likelihood but can't be ignored).

Data queries & quick checks to run (next 24h):
- Zoe: extract per-request kernel-reload events correlated with pod creation timestamps (log pattern: "kernel-loader: select-path"). Query: SELECT count(*) FROM runtime_events WHERE event_type='kernel-reload' AND region IN ('eu-west','apac') AND ts BETWEEN '2029-11-02' AND '2029-11-06';
- Liam: run microbench (short gen, batch size 1..8) against a canary node image with and without the recent node image roll to quantify warmup time delta. Put results in /tmp/latency-experiments-20291106.md
- Daniel: validate NIC error counters and switch logs for EU-West zone 2 on 2029-11-05 08:45-09:30 window. Check for firmware auto-negotiation events.
- Aisha: replay a sampled request profile through a staging balancer that has tighter rate-limiting to simulate queueing and observe tail-latency distribution.

Immediate mitigations tried + results:
- Pinning: temporarily pinned canary capacity to older node image in eu-west-edge pool (rolled back 12 nodes) -> 95th latency reduced ~30% for those nodes after caches warmed.
- Autoscaler cooldown tune: increased scaleDownDelay from 60s -> 180s to avoid oscillation; reduced cold-start incidents in first 2h window.
- Traffic steering: shifted 8% of EU-West traffic to nearby regional pool (eu-north) for 3 hours; overall customer impact minimal, but tail metrics improved.
- Network: applied NIC driver stable config to 6 hosts that showed flaps; flaps stopped on those hosts.

Experiments planned (next iteration):
- Experiment A (Liam): Deploy a runtime build that reduces kernel-reload frequency by keeping a lightweight shared kernel cache and measure token-latency delta. Roll to 20% of new pods in eu-west.
- Experiment B (Zoe + Aisha): Synthetic burst tests with different per-route concurrency caps to find knee for batching windows. Goal: recommend default concurrency tuning for edge balancers.
- Experiment C (Daniel): Run stress with network perturbation emulator (introduce small packet loss and delay) to validate retry amplification hypothesis.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did kernel-reload spikes align so tightly with the node image roll timeline? We need cross-check from release team for image roll batch ID.
- Is there an unobserved client-side retry pattern that multiplies server work? Need rate-limited client trace sampling.
- Could firmware/driver combo in a specific SKU be the root cause for slower DMA under fragmentation? Requires vendor support case if signals persist.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Priya: consolidate this scrapbook and sync with release-engineering about the node-image roll batch (ETA: 2029-11-08).
- Liam: run Experiment A and upload microbench results (ETA: 2029-11-09).
- Zoe: provide dashboard slices and event-annotated timelines for the 95/99 p99 spikes (ETA: 2029-11-07).
- Daniel: collect NIC/switch logs for 12 affected hosts and open a vendor ticket if hardware anomalies found (ETA: 2029-11-08).
- Aisha: schedule canary reroute playbook and document post-mitigation metrics (ETA: 2029-11-07).
- Ops: follow up on INFRA-3245 with nightly updates until resolved.

Notes to self / loose thoughts (informal):
- The pattern smells like a coordination failure: rollout + autoscaler + balancer defaults. Any one alone wouldn't explain kernel-reloads + queue depth + NIC flaps.
- Low-hanging improvement: keep scaleDownCooldown longer for all edge pools during image roll windows (quick policy change).
- Consider making our KV cache rehydrate incremental (warm cache with essential prefixes first) to avoid full cold penalty for short-sequence traffic.

Appendix (links & snippets):
- Snippet from pod log showing kernel selection churn: "2029-11-05T09:03:12Z kernel-loader INFO select-path: kernel-v2.3.7 -> fallback kernel-v2.2.9"
- Quick dashboard: redwood://console/dashboards/edge-latency?from=2029-11-02&to=2029-11-06 (Zoe will snapshot main graph)
- Slack thread: #ops-incident-eu message link: https://slack.com/archives/C0123AB1CD/p1709760000000000

Synthesis for next-week readout (one-liner):
- We have a multi-factor regional tail-latency issue likely caused by coordinated timing between node-image roll, autoscaler oscillation, and edge balancer queue growth; immediate mitigations (pinned nodes + cooldowns + steering) materially reduced tail signals, and a set of experiments are in flight to validate runtime and network contributions.

If you add anything here, add initials and date. This doc is a working scrapbook; we will convert to a formal postmortem if root cause stabilizes.

-- Priya M.
